questions.q: Who authored the book 'Planned Economy for India' in 1934?
questions.why: Sir M. Visvesvaraya published this seminal work advocating for a planned economy in India well before independence.

questions.q: In which year was the National Planning Committee set up under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.why: The committee was formed in 1938 by Subhas Chandra Bose and chaired by Nehru to outline economic plans.

questions.q: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress when the National Planning Committee was formed in 1938?
questions.why: Subhas Chandra Bose initiated the National Planning Committee during his presidency at the Haripura session.

questions.q: The 'Bombay Plan', drafted in 1944, was primarily proposed by:
questions.why: It was a set of proposals for the development of India's post-independence economy drafted by eight leading industrialists.

questions.q: Who formulated the 'People's Plan' in 1945?
questions.why: M.N. Roy, a prominent communist leader, drafted the People's Plan prioritizing agriculture and consumer goods.

questions.q: The 'Gandhian Plan' of 1944 was espoused by:
questions.why: Shriman Narayan Agarwal drafted this plan which focused on agriculture and decentralized village industries.

questions.q: Who drafted the 'Sarvodaya Plan' published in 1950?
questions.why: Inspired by Gandhi and Vinoba Bhave, JP Narayan drafted this plan focusing on agriculture and small-scale industries.

questions.q: The Planning Commission of India was established on:
questions.why: The Planning Commission was established via an executive cabinet resolution on March 15, 1950.

questions.q: The Planning Commission was a/an:
questions.why: It was created by an executive order of the Government of India, not by the Constitution or an Act of Parliament.

questions.q: Who was the first Chairman of the Planning Commission?
questions.why: The Prime Minister of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman, making Nehru the first.

questions.q: Who was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
questions.why: Gulzarilal Nanda served as the first Deputy Chairman, who essentially acts as the executive head of the Commission.

questions.q: The National Development Council (NDC) was established in:
questions.why: The NDC was set up on August 6, 1952, to strengthen and mobilize the effort and resources of the nation in support of the Plan.

questions.q: Which body was responsible for the final approval of the Five Year Plans?
questions.why: The NDC, comprising the PM and state Chief Ministers, was the final approving authority for the Five Year Plans.

questions.q: The First Five Year Plan in India covered the period:
questions.why: The First Plan was launched in 1951 and concluded in 1956, marking the beginning of Indian economic planning.

questions.q: The First Five Year Plan was primarily based on which economic model?
questions.why: It was adapted from the Harrod-Domar model with few modifications, focusing on savings and capital formation.

questions.q: What was the primary focus of the First Five Year Plan?
questions.why: Given the food shortages after partition, agricultural development and irrigation were the top priorities.

questions.q: Which major irrigation project was NOT initiated during the First Five Year Plan?
questions.why: Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud, and Damodar Valley were initiated during the First Plan; Sardar Sarovar came much later.

questions.q: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61) was based on the:
questions.why: Developed by statistician P.C. Mahalanobis, this model emphasized rapid industrialization and heavy industries.

questions.q: The primary objective of the Second Five Year Plan was:
questions.why: The core focus shifted from agriculture to the development of the public sector and rapid industrialization.

questions.q: During which Five Year Plan were steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela established?
questions.why: These major heavy industry projects were the direct result of the Second Plan's industrialization focus.

questions.q: The Durgapur Steel Plant was set up with the assistance of which country?
questions.why: Durgapur in West Bengal was established with British technological and financial collaboration.

questions.q: The Bhilai Steel Plant was established with the collaboration of:
questions.why: Bhilai in Chhattisgarh was built with the assistance of the USSR during the Second Five Year Plan.

questions.q: The Third Five Year Plan covered the period:
questions.why: It followed immediately after the Second Plan, running from 1961 to 1966.

questions.q: The Third Five Year Plan aimed to make the Indian economy:
questions.why: The goal was to reach a 'take-off' stage for a self-generating, self-reliant economy.

questions.q: Which Five Year Plan was deeply affected by the Sino-Indian War of 1962 and Indo-Pak War of 1965?
questions.why: These conflicts, along with a severe drought, severely derailed the Third Plan's economic targets.

questions.q: The period from 1966 to 1969 is known in Indian economic history as:
questions.why: Due to the failure of the Third Plan, regular five-year planning was paused, and three 'Annual Plans' were executed, known as the Plan Holiday.

questions.q: What was the primary reason for declaring the 'Plan Holiday' (1966-69)?
opts: Severe drought and failure of the Third Plan
questions.ansText: Severe drought and failure of the Third Plan
questions.why: Wars, inflation, and a massive drought depleted resources, forcing a temporary halt to five-year planning.

questions.q: The Green Revolution in India was initiated during which period?
questions.why: To combat severe food shortages, High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds were introduced during the Annual Plans (1966-69).

questions.q: The Fourth Five Year Plan covered the period:
questions.why: It resumed after the three-year Plan Holiday, operating from 1969 to 1974 under Indira Gandhi.

questions.q: The two main objectives of the Fourth Five Year Plan were:
opts: Growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance
questions.ansText: Growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance
questions.why: The focus was on recovering from the economic instability of the mid-60s and building self-reliance.

questions.q: During which Five Year Plan did the nationalization of 14 major Indian banks take place (1969)?
questions.why: Indira Gandhi nationalized 14 major commercial banks in 1969, right at the start of the Fourth Plan.

questions.q: The Fifth Five Year Plan was formulated for the period:
questions.why: It was intended to run until 1979 but was terminated prematurely in 1978 by the Janata Party government.

questions.q: Which plan had the overarching objective of 'Garibi Hatao' (Poverty Eradication)?
questions.why: 'Garibi Hatao' was the central political and economic slogan introduced during the Fifth Five Year Plan.

questions.q: Who prepared the draft of the Fifth Five Year Plan?
questions.why: D.P. Dhar drafted the Fifth Plan with a focus on poverty alleviation and attaining self-reliance.

questions.q: The Fifth Five Year Plan was terminated one year early in 1978 by which government?
questions.why: The newly elected Morarji Desai-led Janata Party terminated it early to implement their own Rolling Plan.

questions.q: The Janata Party government introduced which concept in place of Five Year Plans in 1978?
questions.why: The Rolling Plan meant that the performance of the plan was assessed every year, and a new plan was created for the next year.

questions.q: The 'Rolling Plan' concept for developing countries was originally coined by:
questions.why: Gunnar Myrdal proposed this continuous planning concept, which was adapted by the Janata government.

questions.q: The exact duration of the Rolling Plan implemented in India was:
questions.why: It operated for two years until the Congress government returned to power in 1980 and discarded it.

questions.q: The Sixth Five Year Plan covered the period:
questions.why: After returning to power, Indira Gandhi launched the Sixth Plan covering 1980 to 1985.

questions.q: Which Five Year Plan marked the beginning of economic liberalization and an end to Nehruvian socialism?
questions.why: The Sixth Plan initiated gradual economic liberalization, marking a shift away from strict Nehruvian socialist policies.

questions.q: NABARD was established on July 12, 1982, during the:
questions.why: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was formed during the Sixth Plan to boost rural credit.

questions.q: The Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-90) emphasized on:
opts: Modernization, economic growth, and social justice
questions.ansText: Modernization, economic growth, and social justice
questions.why: Under Rajiv Gandhi, the focus shifted strongly to technology upgrading and modernization of industries.

questions.q: Which Five Year Plan saw the launch of the 'Jawahar Rozgar Yojana' (1989)?
questions.why: This massive rural employment program was launched during the final stages of the Seventh Plan.

questions.q: Due to a severe economic crisis and political instability, the Eighth Five Year Plan was delayed. The 'Annual Plans' were executed during:
questions.why: The Balance of Payments crisis and political changes led to two Annual Plans instead of a regular five-year plan.

questions.q: The Eighth Five Year Plan finally covered the period:
questions.why: Launched post-1991 reforms, it ran successfully from 1992 to 1997 under P.V. Narasimha Rao.

questions.q: Which Five Year Plan is associated with the Rao-Manmohan Model of economic reforms?
questions.why: The Eighth Plan was the first to implement the LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, Globalization) reform framework.

questions.q: India's New Economic Policy (LPG reforms) was launched just before the commencement of which plan?
questions.why: The 1991 reforms were introduced during the Annual Plans, setting the foundation for the Eighth Plan in 1992.

questions.q: The primary focus of the Eighth Five Year Plan was:
questions.why: It prioritized employment, education, and public health under the umbrella of human resource development.

questions.q: India became a member of the World Trade Organization (WTO) during the:
questions.why: India joined the WTO on January 1, 1995, perfectly aligning with the Eighth Five Year Plan period.

questions.q: The Ninth Five Year Plan covered the period:
questions.why: Launched during India's 50th year of independence, it operated from 1997 to 2002.

questions.q: What was the central theme of the Ninth Five Year Plan?
opts: Growth with social justice and equity
questions.ansText: Growth with social justice and equity
questions.why: The primary focus was addressing historical inequalities and ensuring economic growth reached all segments of society.

questions.q: The Tenth Five Year Plan covered the period:
questions.why: The Tenth Plan ran from 2002 to 2007 under the leadership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Manmohan Singh.

questions.q: Which plan aimed to double the per capita income of India in the next 10 years?
questions.why: The Tenth Plan uniquely set a massive target to double India's per capita income over a 10-year horizon.

questions.q: The Eleventh Five Year Plan covered the period:
questions.why: Prepared by C. Rangarajan, this plan covered the period from 2007 to 2012.

questions.q: The main theme/objective of the Eleventh Five Year Plan was:
questions.why: The term 'inclusive growth' was centrally highlighted to ensure rural and marginalized participation in the economic boom.

questions.q: The Twelfth Five Year Plan was meant for the period:
questions.why: The Twelfth Plan started in 2012 and concluded its cycle in 2017, effectively ending the Five Year Plan era.

questions.q: What was the central theme of the Twelfth Five Year Plan?
opts: Faster, sustainable and more inclusive growth
questions.ansText: Faster, sustainable and more inclusive growth
questions.why: It added the element of 'sustainability' to the previous plan's theme of inclusive growth.

questions.q: Which was the last Five Year Plan of India?
questions.why: The Twelfth Plan (2012-2017) was the final plan before the system was replaced by NITI Aayog's new strategy documents.

questions.q: The Planning Commission was formally abolished by the Government of India in which year?
questions.why: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the abolition of the Planning Commission in his 2014 Independence Day speech.

questions.q: NITI Aayog came into existence on:
questions.why: Replacing the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog was established on the first day of 2015 as a premier policy think tank.

questions.q: What does 'NITI' stand for in NITI Aayog?
opts: National Institute of Trade and Industry
questions.why: The acronym reflects its mandate to catalyze economic development and foster cooperative federalism.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of NITI Aayog?
questions.why: Much like the old Planning Commission, the Prime Minister serves as the ex-officio Chairman of NITI Aayog.

questions.q: Which sector contributed the most to India's GDP at the beginning of the First Five Year Plan?
questions.why: In 1951, agriculture and allied activities contributed to more than half of India's total Gross Domestic Product.

questions.q: The 'Gadgil Formula' is associated with:
opts: Allocation of central assistance to states
questions.ansText: Allocation of central assistance to states
questions.why: Formulated by D.R. Gadgil, it determined how central plan assistance was distributed among state governments.

questions.q: During which Five Year Plan was the target growth rate achieved and exceeded for the first time?
questions.why: The First Plan targeted 2.1% growth but successfully achieved 3.6%, aided by good monsoons and agricultural yields.

questions.q: In which Five Year Plan was the 'Minimum Needs Programme' introduced?
questions.why: Introduced in 1974, it aimed to provide basic minimum needs like elementary education, water, and healthcare to people.

questions.q: Which plan was based on the 'Input-Output Model'?
questions.why: The Fifth Plan utilized an advanced 'Input-Output Model' combined with a macro-economic growth model.

questions.q: The concept of 'Indicative Planning' was first successfully adopted in which Five Year Plan?
questions.why: Post-1991 liberalization, the Eighth Plan shifted from imperative/command planning to indicative planning for the market economy.

questions.q: During which Five Year Plan did the Green Revolution yield its most significant results leading to self-sufficiency in food grains?
questions.why: Although initiated during the Plan Holiday, the Fourth Plan saw the massive boom in wheat production, securing food self-sufficiency.

questions.q: Which Prime Minister announced the '20-Point Programme' during the Fifth Five Year Plan?
questions.why: Launched in 1975, Indira Gandhi's 20-Point Programme aimed specifically at eradicating poverty and raising living standards.

questions.q: The Bokaro Steel Plant in Jharkhand was established with Soviet assistance during the:
questions.why: Unlike Bhilai and Durgapur (Second Plan), the massive Bokaro Steel Plant was initiated during the Third Plan in 1964.

questions.q: During which Five Year Plan was the Family Planning Programme aggressively implemented, causing widespread public discontent?
questions.why: During the Fifth Plan (coinciding with the Emergency), coercive family planning and forced sterilizations caused massive public backlash.

questions.q: The 'Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana' (PMGSY) was launched during the:
questions.why: Launched in 2000, PMGSY aimed to provide all-weather road connectivity to unconnected rural habitations during the Ninth Plan.

questions.q: The concept of 'Zero Base Budgeting' was first introduced in India during the:
questions.why: Introduced strictly as a planning tool in 1987 under the Seventh Plan, it requires justifying every budgetary expense from zero.

questions.q: The Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) was established in 1956 during the:
questions.why: KVIC was established as a statutory body in April 1957, falling squarely in the early period of the Second Five Year Plan.

questions.q: Who is considered the architect of India's Second Five Year Plan?
questions.why: P.C. Mahalanobis drafted the foundational framework emphasizing rapid industrialization and capital goods production.

questions.q: Which plan experienced the worst failure in terms of achieving its target growth rate, largely due to wars and droughts?
questions.why: Targeted at 5.6%, the Third Plan only achieved 2.8% due to the 1962 China war, 1965 Pakistan war, and severe droughts.

questions.q: Which strategy was adopted in the Seventh Plan to enhance agricultural growth?
questions.why: The Seventh Plan introduced planning based on agro-climatic zones to optimize agricultural potential across diverse geographies.

questions.q: The targeted growth rate of the Twelfth Five Year Plan was initially set at 9%, but was later revised to:
questions.why: Due to global economic slowdowns and domestic hurdles, the NDC revised the ambitious 9% target down to a realistic 8.0%.

questions.q: Instead of Five Year Plans, NITI Aayog prepares:
opts: 3-year action agenda, 7-year strategy document, 15-year vision document
questions.ansText: 3-year action agenda, 7-year strategy document, 15-year vision document
questions.why: NITI Aayog replaced rigid five-year plans with dynamic 15-year visions, broken down into 7-year strategies and 3-year action agendas.

questions.q: Which committee recommended the establishment of the National Development Council (NDC)?
questions.why: The K.C. Neogy Committee of 1946 recommended establishing a planning organization, leading to the creation of the NDC in 1952.

questions.q: In the Harrod-Domar model of the First Plan, economic growth depends primarily on:
questions.why: This macroeconomic model explains that economic growth is a direct result of savings (investment) and the capital-output ratio.

questions.q: The shift from an import-substituting industrialization strategy to export-led growth began in the:
questions.why: The Sixth Plan initiated export promotion and economic liberalization, recognizing the limitations of strict import substitution.

questions.q: 'Operation Flood' (White Revolution) was launched in 1970 during the:
questions.why: The massive dairy development program was launched by NDDB in 1970, falling under the period of the Fourth Five Year Plan.

questions.q: Which Plan laid special emphasis on 'Women's Empowerment' by introducing the concept of a Special Women's Component Plan?
questions.why: The Ninth Plan explicitly mandated that at least 30% of funds in women-related sectors be earmarked for women's development.

questions.q: Which Five Year Plan saw the highest actual growth rate achieved in the history of Indian planning?
questions.why: Despite the 2008 global crisis, the Eleventh Plan achieved a record growth rate of 8.0%, the highest of any plan period.

questions.q: During the First Five Year Plan, community development programs were launched in the year:
questions.why: The Community Development Programme was launched on October 2, 1952, to uplift rural socio-economic life.

questions.q: The highest proportion of plan outlay during the Second Five Year Plan was allocated to:
questions.why: While heavily focused on industry, the highest actual financial outlay (28%) went to building the necessary transport and communication infrastructure.

questions.q: Under which Five Year Plan was the Right to Education Act (RTE) implemented?
questions.why: The RTE Act was passed in 2009 and implemented in April 2010, directly within the Eleventh Five Year Plan timeframe.

questions.q: The concept of 'Inclusive Growth' was explicitly articulated for the first time in the:
questions.why: The Eleventh Plan formally shifted the narrative from mere high growth to 'faster and more inclusive growth'.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Planning Commission: I. It was a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament. II. The Prime Minister served as its ex-officio Chairman. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Statement I is incorrect because the Planning Commission was an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body created by an executive resolution.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the Second Five Year Plan: I. It was based on the Mahalanobis model. II. It prioritized agricultural development over heavy industries. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Statement II is incorrect because the Second Plan explicitly shifted priority away from agriculture and towards heavy industries.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs of Five Year Plans and their major objectives: I. First Plan - Agriculture and Irrigation II. Third Plan - Poverty Eradication (Garibi Hatao) III. Eighth Plan - Human Resource Development. Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.why: Pair II is mismatched; the Third Plan focused on self-reliance, whereas 'Garibi Hatao' was the central theme of the Fifth Plan.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the 'Plan Holiday': I. It was declared between 1966 and 1969. II. During this period, three Annual Plans were executed. III. The Sino-Indian war of 1962 was the sole reason for this holiday. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Statement III is false; severe droughts and the 1965 Indo-Pak war were equally responsible for the economic collapse leading to the holiday.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog: I. It fosters cooperative federalism. II. Chief Ministers of all states are part of its Governing Council. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Both statements are correct; NITI Aayog was specifically designed to ensure states have continuous, institutionalized participation in national policy.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Rolling Plan: I. It was introduced by the Congress government in 1980. II. Under this plan, the performance of the plan is assessed every year and a new plan is made for the next year. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Statement I is wrong; the Rolling Plan was introduced by the Janata Party government in 1978, not the Congress in 1980.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the Eighth Five Year Plan: I. It was the first plan initiated after the economic liberalization of 1991. II. It adopted the strategy of indicative planning. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Both statements are true. It successfully adapted to the new LPG reforms by shifting the state's role to indicative rather than imperative planning.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Twelfth Five Year Plan: I. Its central theme was 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth'. II. It was the final Five Year Plan implemented in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Both statements are correct; it officially closed the era of Five Year Plans under the newly formed NITI Aayog structure.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the National Development Council (NDC): I. It was established in 1952. II. Its primary function was to give final approval to the Five Year Plans. III. The President of India was the Chairman of the NDC. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Statement III is incorrect; the Prime Minister (not the President) served as the ex-officio Chairman of the National Development Council.

questions.q: Consider the following events: I. Establishment of NABARD II. Nationalization of 14 major commercial banks III. Launch of the First Five Year Plan. Arrange these events in the correct chronological order:
questions.why: First Plan was launched in 1951, Banks were nationalized in 1969, and NABARD was established much later in 1982.
